p2.original: 圣雄甘地非暴力学会创始人和主席
p2.en: Founder and President of Mahatma Gandhi Non-Violence Society

p3.original: 上个世纪四十年代，我在南非度过了童年。作为有色人种，生活在执行种族隔离政策的南非并不是很有意思的事情。在那里，肤色随时都可能给你招来无情的刺激。十岁那年，白人打了我，他们认为我太黑了；接着，黑人又打了我，他们认为我太白了。这样的耻辱也许会让任何人想报复社会。
p3.en: I spent my childhood in South Africa in the 1940s. It was not very interesting to live in South Africa as a coloured nation, where apartheid was practised. There, the colour of skin can give you heartless excitement at any time. When I was 10, the whites hit me, and they thought I was too dark. Then the blacks hit me again, and they thought I was too white. Such shame may cause anyone to want revenge on society.

p4.original: 看到我处于悲愤之中，父母决定送我到印度和祖父圣雄甘地（M.K. Gandhi）住一段时间。他们希望我能从祖父那里学到如何面对愤怒、挫折、歧视和耻辱。在接下来的18个月中，我学到的远远超出期待。唯一的遗憾是，那时我还是个普通的孩子，年仅十三岁。如果年纪大一些、聪明一些或更有思想，那么，我就可以学到更多。然而，非暴力生活的一个关键就是：感激生活的赐予，而不贪心。我怎么可以忘记这一点呢？
p4.en: Seeing me in a state of sadness, my parents decided to send me to stay with my grandfather, M.K. Gandhi, for a while. They wanted me to learn from their grandfather how to face anger, frustration, discrimination and shame. In the next 18 months, I have learned far more than I expected. The only regret was that I was a regular kid, only 13 years old. If I'm older, smart or thinkier, then I can learn more. However, a key to a non-violent life is to be grateful for the gift of life without greed. How can I forget that?

p5.original: 和祖父在一起的日子里，我意识到什么是真正的非暴力以及认识自身暴力的重要性。由于缺乏了解，我们常常认识不到自身的暴力。我们认为，只有打人、鞭挞、杀人以及战争等才算是暴力，而这类事与我们无关。
p5.en: On a day with my grandfather, I realized what was truly non-violence and the importance of recognizing my own violence. We often fail to recognize our own violence because of a lack of understanding. In our view, only beating, whipping, killing and war are acts of violence that are not our concern.

p6.original: 为了加深我对暴力的认识，祖父让我画一棵树，类似家族树，用以描述暴力的根源。他认为，认识暴力，有助于理解非暴力。每天晚上，他和我一起分析我一天中的经历——我的所读、所看、所做。如果某个行为涉及使用武力，就把它归到暴力之树“身体的暴力”那一边；如果主要造成精神伤害，那就归到暴力之树“隐蔽的暴力”那一边。
p6.en: To deepen my understanding of violence, my grandfather asked me to draw a tree, similar to a family tree, to describe the root causes of violence. He believes that knowledge of violence contributes to understanding non-violence. Every night, he analyses with me the experience of my day — what I read, what I see, what I do. If an act involves the use of force, it is placed on the side of the “physical violence” of the tree of violence; If it is mainly psychological, it falls to the “hidden violence” side of the tree of violence.

p7.original: 几个月后，我房间的一面墙上就写满了各种“隐蔽的暴力”。与“身体的暴力”相比，它们的危害性不那么明显，但祖父认为它们更为有害。他解释说，归根结底，是“隐蔽的暴力”激怒了受害者，使他作出暴力的反抗——不管是以个人的名义，还是以团体成员的名义。如果看不到这一点，我们为促进和平所做的努力，要么徒劳无功，要么昙花一现。不切断地狱之火的燃料供应，怎么可能成功灭火呢？
p7.en: A few months later, a wall in my room was filled with “hidden violence”. They are less harmful than “physical violence”, but grandfather considered them more harmful. He explained that, in the final analysis, it was the “hidden violence” that provoked the victim to mount violent resistance, whether in the name of individuals or of members of groups. If that is not seen, our efforts to promote peace will be either futile or fruitless. How can we put out the fire without cutting off the fuel supply of Hellfire?

p8.original: 祖父反复强调在交流中运用非暴力原则的重要性。许多年来，通过著书和开设研讨班，卢森堡博士倾力介绍非暴力沟通，作出了令人钦佩的贡献。带着浓厚的兴趣，我阅读了本书。这本书的深度和简洁给我留下了深刻的印象。
p8.en: Grandfather repeatedly stressed the importance of applying the principle of non-violence in communication. For many years, through books and seminars, the Dr. Luxembourg has made an admirable contribution by making an excellent presentation on Nonviolent Communication. With a great interest, I read a book. I was impressed by the depth and simplicity of the book.

p9.original: 祖父曾提倡：“让梦想中的世界通过我们的转变得以实现。”我相信，除非从我做起，我们的梦想就不可能实现。不幸的是，我们总是希望别人先开始改变。
p9.en: My grandfather once advocated: “Let the dream world be realized through our transformation. I believe that our dreams cannot be realized unless I do so. Unfortunately, we always want others to start changing first.

p10.original: 非暴力不是今天用了、明天就可以抛弃的权宜之计。非暴力也不是让你变得温顺或听话。非暴力主张积极进取，而非消极无为。人们习惯于围绕个人利益采取行动。在基于狭隘个人主义、物质至上的当代社会，更是如此。视非暴力为权宜之计或对他人的顺从，并无益于家庭、社区和国家的和谐。
p10.en: Non-violence is not a stopgap measure that is used today and can be abandoned tomorrow. Non-violence doesn't make you gentle or obedient. Non-violence advocates positive progress rather than passive inaction. People are accustomed to acting in the interests of individuals. This is particularly true in contemporary societies based on narrow individualism and material supremacy. Treating non-violence as an expediency or submissiveness to others does not contribute to the harmony of the family, the community and the State.

p11.original: 在国家危急时刻，能否挥舞国旗聚集在一起，并不重要；成为超级大国，拥有多次毁灭地球的能力，不足以解决问题；通过军事力量，征服世界其他地区，也于事无补——因为恐惧无法带来和平。
p11.en: It is not important that in times of national crisis, the flag should come together; Being a super-Power with the capacity to destroy the planet many times is not enough to solve the problem; Conquering the rest of the world through military force is not helping — fear cannot bring about peace.

p12.original: 非暴力意味着让爱融入生活。让尊重、理解、欣赏、感激、慈悲和友情，而非自私自利、贪婪、憎恨、偏见、怀疑和敌意，来主导生活。人们常说：这是一个弱肉强食的世界，为了生存，我们必须不择手段。这个观点，请恕我无法同意。
p12.en: Non-violence means integrating love into life. Let respect, understanding, appreciation, gratitude, compassion and friendship, rather than selfishness, greed, hatred, prejudice, suspicion and hostility, dominate life. It is often said that this is a world where the weak are strong and we must do whatever is necessary to survive. I beg your pardon, I cannot agree with that.

p13.original: 如果今天的世界是无情的，那是我们的生活方式造成它的无情。我们的转变与世界的状态息息相关。而改变沟通方式是自我转变的重要开端。我推荐大家阅读这本书，并运用它介绍的沟通方法。我深信，提升沟通品质有助于建设一个友爱的世界。
p13.en: If today's world is ruthless, it is our way of life that has caused it to be ruthless. Our transformation is closely linked to the state of the world. Change of communication is an important start to self-change. I recommend that you read the book and use the communication methods it introduces. I am convinced that improving the quality of communication will help build a world of fraternity.
